plugins.name: botling.board
plugins.title: Pins
plugins.description: Pin a component to a bot: a chip above the input box (and the sheet it raises) or a small card floating in a corner of the window. It keeps the pins and runs their commands once you allowed them.

plugins.name: botling.cards
plugins.title: Cards
plugins.description: The app's own cards in the chat: the web preview card (網頁預覽卡片) shows a one-page HTML result small, with a button to open it full size. A component of the same name in the library replaces it.

plugins.name: botling.catchup
plugins.title: Chat summaries
plugins.description: Coming back to a chat with many unread replies folds them into one card with a short summary; stretches between your messages can be summarized too. Each point links back to the messages it comes from. Settings → General → Chat summaries.

settings.title: Summary prompt
settings.value: Write short bullets covering what finished, what is still running, and anything waiting for the user's decision (put that last, starting it with "!! "). Keep ids, numbers and names exactly as written.
settings.default: Write short bullets covering what finished, what is still running, and anything waiting for the user's decision (put that last, starting it with "!! "). Keep ids, numbers and names exactly as written.

plugins.name: botling.chat-extras
plugins.title: Chat extras
plugins.description: Pictures in a row become one gallery, a long message of yours folds to its first lines, and a long paste waits as a chip above the input box.

settings.title: Collapse pastes over (characters; 0 turns it off)
Collapse pastes over (lines; 0 turns it off)

plugins.name: botling.component-studio
plugins.title: Component studio
plugins.description: Turns a reply into a component: "Make into component" under a reply (or on a result page's preview card), a bot's own <suggest-component> chip, and the spec workspace in the right panel where you and Maintainer shape it.

plugins.name: botling.deps
plugins.title: Plugin dependencies
plugins.description: A read-only board of who depends on whom among the plugins: every plugin (built in and installed) with its version and whether it is on, the services it provides, requires or uses, the screen slots it fills, and arrows from each plugin to the ones that provide what it needs, with a missing provider in red. It only looks; it never turns anything on or off.

plugins.name: botling.design
plugins.title: Claude Design
plugins.description: /design in the input box: the bot makes a Claude Design on claude.ai and replies with its link.

plugins.name: botling.dev
plugins.title: Developer tools
plugins.description: For the project that is Botling's own source (Settings → Developer): its manager may install a build it made (<install-build>, you confirm on a card, a build that does not come up is rolled back by itself) and see the app's window (<app-screenshot/>), and hears how in its instructions.

plugins.name: botling.git
plugins.title: Git
plugins.description: App-managed git worktrees for a project's work (a branch and folder the agent works in, merged or discarded when you say so), the Review of their changes (diffs, comments sent to the agent, per-turn changes) and committing and opening a pull request from it.

plugins.name: botling.note
plugins.title: Note
plugins.description: A Note tab in each bot's header: edit the bot's own markdown note (.bot/note.md) in place; a line renders as markdown (images, KaTeX math, code, lists) once the cursor leaves it; follows the app's light/dark theme. One note can fork into routes (route tabs, a route overview, `<!-- branch / route -->` comments in the same note.md); a + button and the / menu insert headings, to-dos and images. A cell is a whole chunk of Markdown, cut by `<!-- cell -->` lines (a note without them is one cell per route); each cell is framed with a colored bar by type, can be dragged by its grip (into the route a branch shows, out of a branch, between routes, up/down; Cmd+Z undoes it) and has a toolbar to split at the cursor (Ctrl+Shift+-), merge with the next (Ctrl+Shift+M), insert, move (also into and out of branches), delete and change type (Markdown, code, math). Markdown (GFM pipe) tables render as real tables (header, borders, column alignment) and are edited cell by cell in place (Tab / Shift+Tab, Enter adds a row, a hover bar and right-click menu add or delete rows and columns, "/表格" inserts one); the file keeps tidy pipe-table text and untouched tables keep their bytes. Whole lines can be selected across lines, cells and tables (mouse drag, Shift+click, Shift+arrows; Cmd+A selects the cell, again the whole shown note); Cmd+C copies the Markdown (no cell, branch or route lines; only the shown routes), and typing or Delete replaces the selection (Cmd+Z undoes it). Each branch remembers its own shown route, nested branches per parent route (switching a branch away and back brings back the deeper routes chosen there), and the app keeps those choices and the cursor / scroll per note across tab switches and restarts (plugin storage, never note.md). A `<show name="…">JSON</show>` (or `<show name="…" command="…"></show>`) on its own line(s), as the chat writes it, is drawn as a live card in a cell of its own (the note keeps the plain text): a card with a Command runs it once allowed (th

plugins.name: botling.orchestration
plugins.title: Orchestration rules
plugins.description: The advice bots are given on how to hand out work, follow up and review reports (rules.json: one text per policy sentence of Botling's own rules). Read-only and pinned: Botling uses it only while rules.json is byte for byte the one it shipped with, else its own copy of the same words. Contract sentences (what the app does and guards) are not in it and cannot be changed by it.

plugins.name: botling.pin-area
plugins.title: Pin 區
plugins.description: Pin 區: a thin list of pinned task cards above the chat, one row per card (a card that waits for you has an orange edge; more than 4 cards show the first rows and one 「還有 N 件」 row). A click opens the row in place into the card, kept at the top while the chat scrolls below it: the card's one-line status (rewritten in place, with what it said before), its steps, its thread and a folded 過程 · N 則更新 log. The card has no input box: the chat's own box gets a 「回覆到 <card>」 chip, and what you type goes into the card. Esc, the chip's ✕, the chevron or a click on the chat's empty space close it. You pin any message from its 釘選 button; a bot may pin a card too, but only for a run of 10 minutes or more or when it needs you, and may rewrite the status line of its own cards (the <pin-card> reply tag) and answer in a card's thread (<pin-say>). Typing @ in the input box also offers the cards: "@card words" goes into that card's thread, and the bot's answer lands there. A worker or sub bot a card follows (<pin-card worker="task_id">) rewrites that card's status line when it reports, and the report lands in the card's "N updates", not in the chat. Plain messages in a chat that has cards carry a note of the cards (their ids, titles, states) and may be sorted by the app afterwards (off until you turn it on in Settings › Plugins › Pin 區: your line is sent at once and never waits; one call of a small model with no tools, which model is a setting, decides beside it): a line that clearly belongs to a card is moved into it together with the bot's reply, and the chat keeps one line with 移回聊天 and 改到… (one tap each); a new card or the merge of two cards is only suggested, and waits for your tap; anything unsure stays in the chat. A worker a bot named for a card (app_handoff group = the card's title) reports into that card, and the chat keeps one line; a card done for an hour puts itself away (釘回 brings it back). Unpinning leaves a 釘回 to put it back; a done card you opened and closed unpins itself

plugins.name: botling.report
plugins.title: Reports
plugins.description: Report pages for the bots: a skill (the ReportSpec v2 guide) and a command (Botling 2 --render-report spec.json page.html) that renders one, with the rule that tells every bot to use them.

plugins.name: botling.routines
plugins.title: Routines
plugins.description: The Routines button in the chat header: a bot's schedules (its routines.cron lines and the app's own one-time and recurring ones), with Pause, Resume and Cancel. Botling still keeps and runs the schedules; this plugin only lists them and asks for the change.

plugins.name: botling.terminal
plugins.title: Terminal
plugins.description: A shell in the bot's project folder under the chat: the Terminal button in the chat header (Mod+J) shows tabs of real shells, one list per bot, kept running while the panel is hidden.

plugins.name: botling.usage
plugins.title: Usage
plugins.description: What the bots used: the subscription quota rings in the sidebar gear's popover (Claude, Codex, Antigravity) and Settings → Usage (cost and tokens today, limits, by bot, earlier days). The numbers are read by Botling; this plugin only shows them.

plugins.name: botling.whiteboard
plugins.title: Whiteboard
plugins.description: The main bot's whiteboard: every bot's card (what waits on you, what runs, what is idle), numbers, charts and each bot's report, in a tab beside Chat and Board. A bot may give its card a small picture with <whiteboard>.

plugins.name: ccb-latex
plugins.title: LaTeX
plugins.description: Typesets $…$, $$…$$, \(…\) and \[…\] in messages with KaTeX, previews formulas while you type, and copies formulas as TeX.

plugins.name: acme-board
plugins.title: Acme Board
plugins.description: A fixture in the old ccb shape.
